subtopics.content: a. Source of food (meat, milk, eggs, honey etc.)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss farm animals as a source of food

subtopics.content: b. Raw materials e.g. hide and skin, bones, hooves, hair/fur, egg shells
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss farm animals as a source of raw materials

subtopics.content: c. Source of manure (fertilizer, biogas, bio fuel), growing of maggots and earthworms
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss farm animals as a source of manure and related uses

subtopics.content: d. Source of feed ingredients - blood meal, bone meal, meat and bone meal, snail shell, egg shell, feathers etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss farm animals as a source of feed ingredients

subtopics.content: e. Animal power (animal traction, transportation)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss animal power

subtopics.content: f. Research (laboratory, field), drugs, vaccines, hormones etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss the use of farm animals in research and drug production

subtopics.content: g. Source of employment; sales of products and by-products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss employment and income from farm animals

subtopics.content: h. Social functions e.g. payment of bride price, cultural displays (weddings)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss the social functions of farm animals

subtopics.content: i. Security e.g. ducks, bees, turkeys; pets e.g. rabbits, sheep, chickens
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss the use of farm animals for security and as pets

subtopics.content: j. Sports and games e.g. horse racing, chicken fighting; religious festivals e.g. turkeys, rams etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss the use of farm animals in sports, games and religious festivals

subtopics.content: k. Source of foreign exchange through export of animal products and by-products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss foreign exchange earnings from animal products

subtopics.content: a. Classification of farm animals: simple stomach (non-ruminant or monogastric) e.g. poultry (avian), pig (swine), rabbits, horses, donkeys, snails, bees, grasscutters; complex stomach (polygastric or ruminants) i.e. cattle, sheep and goat
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify farm animals based on stomach type

subtopics.content: b. Identification of ruminants and non-ruminants
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the external features of common ruminants and non-ruminants and differentiate them based on type of stomach and type of feed consumed

topics.title: Internal organs and their functions in farm animals

subtopics.content: a. Internal organs e.g. liver, lungs, heart, kidney, spleen, pancreas, stomach, crop, caecum, gizzard, small intestine, large intestine, tongue etc., and their functions
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the internal organs of farm animals and state their functions

topics.title: Body systems and their functions in farm animals

subtopics.content: a. Digestive, respiratory, nervous, circulatory, skeletal and reproductive systems
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the functions of each body system

subtopics.content: a. Definition of terms used in livestock reproduction
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define terms such as ovulation, oestrus cycle, heat period, signs of heat, mating, gestation, parturition, lactation, colostrum, flushing, steaming up, dystocia, vaginal prolapse etc.

subtopics.content: b. Reproduction in livestock (mammals)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss detection of heat, mating systems, pregnancy detection and signs of parturition

subtopics.content: c. Reproduction in poultry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the process of egg formation in poultry

subtopics.content: d. Reproductive hormones and their functions
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the sources and roles of female hormones (oestrogen, progesterone, relaxin, oxytocin etc.) and male hormones (testosterone/androgen)

subtopics.content: e. Management of pregnant farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss regular and adequate feeding, body exercise, steaming up, separation from male animals, provision of clean and adequate water, administration of drugs where necessary, dipping to eliminate ecto-parasites, and parturition

subtopics.content: a. Intensive, semi-intensive and extensive systems
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the livestock management systems and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each

subtopics.content: a. Housing requirements for each of the farm animals, using local materials for construction of animal houses
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss housing requirements and use of local materials for construction

subtopics.content: b. Other management practices: feeding, sanitation, hygiene, castration, dehorning, deworming, vaccination, inoculation, culling, debeaking, smoking (in bees), docking (detailing), means of identification (tattooing, branding, ear-notching, rings etc.), isolation, weaning, care of the young animal until weaned
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand these practices and discuss the importance of each

subtopics.content: c. Simple record keeping including income and expenditure accounts
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to keep simple records and income and expenditure accounts

subtopics.content: d. Management from birth to maturity of a named large ruminant, small ruminant, poultry, pigs, grasscutter, bees and snails
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss management practices from birth to maturity of the named animals

topics.title: Meaning and classes of animal feeds

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of animal nutrition, feed nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats and oil, vitamins, minerals and water), their functions, sources and deficiencies in farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss animal nutrition and feed nutrients, their functions, sources and deficiencies

subtopics.content: b. Classification of animal feeds into concentrates, roughages, supplements, feed additives etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify animal feeds

subtopics.content: a. Livestock rations: meaning and types (balanced, maintenance, production rations)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the meaning and types of livestock rations

subtopics.content: b. Malnutrition: meaning, causes, symptoms and practical ways to check it
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss practical ways to check malnutrition such as feeding balanced rations, feeding weaker animals separately, deworming, giving supplementary feeds, adding feed additives to stimulate appetite, protecting animals from toxic plants and harmful substances, adjusting stocking rates and providing good quality and adequate water

subtopics.content: a. Practical diet formulations for the different classes of farm animals (starter, grower and finisher diets)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to carry out practical diet formulations for the different classes of farm animals

subtopics.content: b. Feed ingredients e.g. blood meal, fish meal, cotton seed cake, oyster shell, groundnut cake, maize grains, salt, premix, glycine etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify different feed ingredients used for diet formulation

subtopics.content: c. Factors to consider in feed formulation: physiological status of animal, species, age, body weight, production target, acceptability of feed, nutrient composition of the feed, ingredient availability, cost of feed ingredients etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the factors to consider in feed formulation

topics.title: Processing and marketing of animal products

subtopics.content: a. Processing techniques for different farm animal products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know pre-slaughtering, slaughtering and post-slaughtering activities, hygienic conditions in processing, slaughtering techniques for different farm animals, and processing of products e.g. egg, milk, meat, skin, wool, honey, snail shell, feathers, fur, hooves, horns, blood, faeces/droppings into other forms (value addition)

subtopics.content: b. Marketing of animal products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand common marketing channels and agents such as producers, wholesalers, retailers, consumers, and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each

sections.sectionTitle: Section C: Pasture and Range Management

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance of pasture and forage crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss the definition, examples and importance of pasture and forage crops

subtopics.content: b. Types of pasture and forage crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the types and features of pasture and forage crops

subtopics.content: c. Terminologies in pasture management
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know basic terminologies in pasture management

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and characteristics of rangelands
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the meaning and features of rangeland

subtopics.content: b. Methods of rangeland improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know methods: reseeding, rotational grazing, controlled stocking, deferred grazing, controlled burning, fertilizer application, pest control, disease control etc.

subtopics.content: c. Importance of rangeland
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the role of rangeland in livestock production e.g. provision of vegetation and grasses for animals, exercise, provision of hay and silage

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of animal improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the meaning and terminologies used in animal improvement

subtopics.content: b. Aims/importance of farm animal improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the aims: high reproductive efficiency, potency, mothering ability, cool temperament, high libido, resistance to pests and diseases, tolerance to harsh environment etc.

subtopics.content: a. Methods used in farm animal improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss introduction, selection and breeding

subtopics.content: b. Merits and demerits of methods used in farm animal improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the merits and demerits of each method

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of artificial insemination
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the term artificial insemination

subtopics.content: b. Methods of artificial insemination
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify materials, methods, steps and precautions in carrying out artificial insemination

subtopics.content: c. Advantages of artificial insemination
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the advantages of artificial insemination

subtopics.content: a. Concept of farm animal disease
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the meaning and causal agents (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa) of diseases in farm animals

subtopics.content: b. General symptoms of diseases in farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss signs of a sick animal e.g. loss of appetite, loss of weight, diarrhoea, high body temperature, blood stained urine, gnashing of teeth, discharges from natural openings, blood stained faeces, ruffled feathers or fur, standing hair, undue noise, excessive salivation, anaemia, staggering gait, difficulty in breathing, coma, sudden death

subtopics.content: c. Diseases of farm animals, prevention and control
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the main diseases, causal agents, mode of transmission and symptoms, and know simple preventive and control measures including use of antibiotics and ethno-veterinary practices

subtopics.content: d. Factors predisposing farm animals to diseases
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know factors e.g. poor nutrition, poor health status, poor sanitation, inadequate bio-security, overcrowding, unfavourable weather conditions, low immunity

subtopics.content: a. Livestock parasites
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the meaning, classes, control/prevention and effects of parasites, including life cycles, and identify ecto-parasites (ticks, lice, mites, fleas etc.) and endo-parasites (tapeworm, roundworm, hookworm, pinworm, liver fluke, trypanosome etc.) and their economic importance

subtopics.content: b. Livestock pests
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know livestock pests (rodents, snakes, soldier ants, birds, weevils, termites, flies etc.), prevention/control using dewormers, acaricides, pesticides and ethno-veterinary practices, effects of pests on farm animals, and identify and know the economic importance of storage pests (rodents, weevils, termites, cockroaches) and field pests (soldier ants, birds, snakes, flies)

topics.title: Products and by-products of farm animals

subtopics.content: 1. Products and by-products of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify and know the uses of products and by-products such as meat, eggs, milk, honey, hides, skin, blood, hair, wool, feathers, horn, hooves, bones, snail shell, animal dung

subtopics.content: 2. Identification of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe, draw and label the external parts of farm animals

topics.title: Internal organs and their functions in farm animals

subtopics.content: 3. Internal organs and their functions in farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify and draw the major internal structures in the various body systems of a named ruminant, poultry and pig, and state the differences in structures and functions

topics.title: Tools and equipment used in management of farm animals

subtopics.content: 4. Tools and equipment used in management of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify tools and equipment for: housing (head pan, trowel, shovel/spade, hammer, pincers, pliers, spanner, screw driver); brooding (coal pots, kerosene stoves, hurricane lantern, electric bulb, hover, chick feeder, flat trays, chick drinker, brood guard/surround, thermometer, hygrometer); feeding (feeders, drinkers, weighing scale); identification (branding iron, ear clips, neck chains, marker, ear notcher, indelible ink); debeaking (debeaking machine, sharp knife, heater); castration (surgical blade/scalpel, burdizzo, elastrator, elastic ring, cotton wool, suture needle, suture thread); handling (kraal, restraining ropes, wooden rod, nose ring); dehorning (iron saw, knife/cutlass); incubation (incubator, hatcher, chick box, egg tray, humidifier, candler); milking (cheese cloth, milking machine, milking chute, milk testing cup, drenching bottle, milking pails, buckets); slaughtering (cutlass, knife, stunning gun, electric shocker, defeathering machine, eviscerator, conveyor, weighing scale, blast freezer, cold rooms); pasture and forage crops (sickle, knife/cutlass, harvesters, silo); and discuss their maintenance

subtopics.content: 5. Feeds and feedstuffs
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify and know the uses of feeds and feedstuffs such as common feed ingredients (maize, groundnut cake, soya bean meal, palm kernel cake, fish meal, bone meal, oyster shell, limestone, salt, salt lick, premix, wheat offal), crop residues, agricultural by-products and non-conventional feeds (jack bean, rumen digesta, cassava peel) and the major nutrients they contain

subtopics.content: 6. Pasture and forage crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify common pasture and forage crops and know their uses, and discuss hay and silage making

subtopics.content: 7. Artificial insemination
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the tools and equipment and their uses, and discuss simple techniques of semen collection, preservation and insemination

topics.title: Pests and parasites of farm animals

subtopics.content: 8a. Pests of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify storage pests (rodents, weevils, termites, cockroaches) and field pests (soldier ants, birds, snakes, flies) and know their economic importance

subtopics.content: 8b. Parasites of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify ectoparasites (ticks, lice, mites, fleas) and endoparasites (tapeworm, roundworms, hookworm, pinworm, liver fluke, trypanosomes), know their economic importance, and study their life cycles, prevention and control
